bio: Ernest William Radford (1857–1919) was an English poet, critic and socialist, a follower of William Morris and an organiser of the Arts and Crafts movement.
The poems here are taken from Arthur Quiller-Couch's anthology The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (Clarendon Press, 1912).

poems.title: Quiet
poems.author: Ernest Radford
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Tired brain, there is a place of rest
On the broad bosom of the land
Where quiet will reward the quest.
The dinning of the iron hand
Will be unheard; ah! there shall we

Have with the noise of tumbling rills,
And with the music of the sea,
The quiet that my dream fulfils
Of Quiet, aching tho' it be.
